Welcome to The Trumans Eagles Nest
Find that sweet spot where life slows down... and the fish are always biting.
Home
Other Properties
Fisherman's Roost

Honeyhole RV Park
Stay near Missouri's best fishing
Just minutes from Bucksaw and Long Shoal Marina
We boast some of the areas largest and most secluded RV pads along with open areas for you to build your carport overhead. Partial shade is available to enjoy at times while still being able to soak up the sun. Full shade is available in some spots with the surrounding trees on our large lots.
Fishing
Trumans Eagles Nest is located just minutes from Bucksaw Marina... the gateway to some amazing fishing.
Camping
Our park is open year around, so there is no need to remove your camper or store it elsewhere in the off season. We also offer nightly camping spots.
Nature
If you need a place away from the bright lights and big cities... look no further than Trumans Eagles Nest. There is plenty to explore on our 20 acre park and even more on the 50,000 acres of bordering core land.

Recreation admission fees and memberships
Visitors to Lakewood recreation centers can pay a one-time admission fee or choose from a variety of cost-saving passes and memberships. Admission is free for those with insurance-based memberships; view the section below to learn more.
Passes can be purchased in-person at recreation centers or online.

Insurance-Based Memberships
Insurance-based memberships are fitness programs offered to adults and older adults via insurance companies. They offer great benefits at Lakewood Recreation Centers and the Clements Community Center. Always check with your insurance provider to see if you qualify.
If you have questions regarding these memberships, contact a Lakewood staff member at Kimberly.Borawa@lakewoodco.gov or call 303-987-5420 .
Insurance Membership FAQs
1. What is an insurance-based membership?
An insurance-based membership is a type of membership that is based off of your insurance. The most common memberships are for those 65 and up, but there are a number of other programs offered for those 18 and up. Most of these insurance perks will cover your membership to the recreation centers in Lakewood.
2. What are the benefits?
Please see the benefits section above this page for a full listing.
2. How do I know which program I’m eligible for?
Each plan differs between insurance companies, and also between members on the same insurance plan. To make sure you are eligible, we recommend calling your insurance provider before coming in to the recreation center. Ask which program(s) your insurance provider participates in and if you specifically are eligible.
3. What is the difference between the programs?
All of the insurance-based membership programs offer the same benefits. The only differences come from the insurance providers and who is included in each program. Some insurance providers have specific requirements (such as monthly attendance) in order to stay in the program and receive the benefits.
4. Which fitness classes are included?
All general admission fitness classes are included in all of the insurance-based membership programs. Visit Lakewood.org/Fitness for a list of classes and schedules. All aqua fitness classes are also included, except Aqua Ai Chi & GlideFit. You will also get 20% off all registration classes such as mind/body classes and strength-based classes.
5. My insurance provider says I’m eligible for one of the programs. How do I sign up?
First, make sure you have contacted your insurance provider by calling the number on the back of your insurance card and check that you are eligible for the fitness/wellness programs they participate in.
If you are eligible, then you can come into any Lakewood recreation center and get signed up for your membership at the front desk. Please bring your insurance information and the name of the program you are eligible for.
The front desk will then verify your eligibility with the program you have been qualified for through your insurance and get your facility membership set up.
6. If I’m not eligible for any of the programs through my insurance, what other options do I have?
a. If you are 62 or older, you can sign up for Lakewood’s Senior All Access pass, which has all of the same benefits as the insurance-based membership programs excluding free facility access. This type of membership is discounted from a regular senior membership and includes aqua fitness classes (except Ai Chi & GlideFit). You can sign up for this pass at the front desk of any Lakewood recreation center.
b. The Lakewood Possibilities Fund (LPF) gives scholarships to households with lower incomes, which can be used for programs and facility access. Possibilities Fund scholarships are awarded based on household income, and a portion of the registration fee is always paid by the participant. Lakewood Residents that qualify can receive up to $300 scholarship assistance per family member annually based on need and available funding.
c. If you do not qualify for any of the options above, you will need to get a facility membership or sign-up for a session of any of our registration programs.
7. Can other family members use my pass?
No - your insurance only covers you and your activity. If a family member is covered under your insurance, contact your insurance provider to see if they are eligible for an insurance-based membership program as well.
8. Can I bring a guest(s) with my pass?
A guest can come in to any Lakewood recreation center and request a guest form from the front desk to try out any of our general admission fitness classes for free the first time. After that, they will need to pay a daily drop-in fee.
9. I have SilverSneakers through United Healthcare now. Will I have RenewActive in 2020?
The United Healthcare Medicare Advantage plan will be switching from SilverSneakers to RenewActive as of January 1, 2020. To make sure you are still eligible for an insurance-based membership program during this transition, contact your insurance provider to see if you are eligible for RenewActive. After January 1, you will need to go to the front desk of any Lakewood recreation center to switch your membership information. You will still get all of the same benefits under RenewActive that you did under SilverSneakers.
10. I’m switching my insurance plans. Do I need to update my information at the recreation center?
Yes. Visit the front desk of any Lakewood recreation center to give them your new information and switch insurance-based membership programs if you have already been told by your insurance provider that you are still eligible for a program that Lakewood participates in.
11. If I’m eligible for Medicare, can I automatically enrolled in a program?
Most insurance-based membership programs accept Medicare regardless of age, but you will still need to check with your insurance provider to see if you qualify for any of the programs Lakewood participates in.
Benefits
Free admission to all four Lakewood recreation centers .
Free general admission fitness classes: View the schedule .
Free admission to most aqua fitness classes.
20% discount on all registration fitness classes, like Pilates, BodyPump and Yoga.
Free orientations on your benefits and what you can access through these programs. Contact NicSch@lakewood.org or 303-987-5448
for more information.
List of memberships
Always check with your insurance provider to see if you qualify.
ADULT MEMBERSHIPS (ages 18-64)
Active&Fit Direct
Active&Fit Direct by American Specialty Health Fitness, Inc, allows members to access benefits for a monthly fee. You must be a member of a commercial employer group or individual plan to use this program.
Prime
The Prime Fitness Program by Tivity Health is available through participating sponsors — often this is through an employer health plan.
OLDER ADULT MEMBERSHIPS
SilverSneakers
The well-known SilverSneakers Fitness Program by Tivity Health is specifically designed to encourage eligible members to increase their level of activity and motivate them to continue to be active. If you are Medicare-eligible, check with your insurance provider to see if your plan qualifies you.
Silver&Fit
Silver&Fit by Ashlink is designed specifically to help older adults achieve better health through regular exercise and health education. If you are Medicare-eligible, check with your insurance provider to see if your plan qualifies you.
RenewActive
RenewActive from UnitedHealthcare is available with select Medicare Advantage plans. Designed around you and your goals, RenewActive offers access to participating fitness locations, both local and national options and group fitness classes, as well as online brain exercises to help keep both your body and your mind active — all at no additional cost.
Senior All-Access
This City of Lakewood membership is available to any adult ages 62 and older. It offers the same benefits that insurance memberships provide.
Cost one person:
- Annual Pass: $350 resident, $400 nonresident.
- Monthly Pass: $29 resident, $33 nonresident.
Cost household (2 people):
- Annual Pass: $600 resident, $684 nonresident.
- Monthly Pass: $50 resident, $57 nonresident.
Membership can be paid in monthly installments.
Financial assistance is available for qualified applicants via the Lakewood Possibilities Fund. Learn More

About Six Lakes Resort
About Us
OUR APPROACH
Our vision is to make Six Lakes Resort an outstanding resort in Chetek, Wisconsin. We want to keep this a family run business as much as possible. We plan to make our family memories here and hope to expand our family to all of the residents at Six Lakes Resort. We hope the residents come back year after year and make as many memories as we will.
OUR STORY
Josh and Lisa have been married for 14 years and are always looking for new adventures. Our most recent adventure is the purchase of Six Lakes Resort. Josh’s parents had always dreamed of owning a resort in Chetek. They have been coming to Chetek for decades. We love every part of making this dream come true. You will see our children at the resort during the season. Emma is 13, River is 10 and Ryker is 8. They have made many memories here already but there are so many more memories to come. We plan on running this resort long into our retirement.

Seasonal Camping
For seasonal camping, we will be open mid April thru October 5th weather permitting October 14th. So water may or may not be on at open or close.
All seasonal site fees are due in full by March 15, as well as dock fees. Late fees may apply after March 15th of $5.00 a day.
No seasonal rent will be refunded once the season has started.
Park guidelines
1. Campsite check-out time: 12 pm
2. Pets are welcome when accompanied by a responsible owner. Pets must be leashed, cleaned up after and quiet. Nuisance pets will be asked to leave the park with their owners. Pet owners assume liability for their pets action.
3. Quiet hours 11 pm – 8 am
4. Swimming is at your own risk. No lifeguard on duty
5. Campfires are allowed at campsites only when attended and protected at all times. Do not leave trash in campfire rings.
6. No firewood sold after 8:30 pm. Please plan ahead
7. Garbage pickup is on Fridays and Mondays; place trash in dumpsters before 6 am on these days
8. Help to protect our wildlife and trees. Do Not cut or carve trees. Obey all fishing laws and regulations.
9. You must be at least 21 years old to rent boats at Six Lakes Resort. All boating passengers must have a life jacket. Seat cushions are no longer legal flotation devices.
10. Speed limit is 5 miles per hour . Drive cautiously through the campground as there are many small campers also. If you do not maintain 5 mph or less you will be asked to leave the premises.
11. Children should be under adult supervision while in restrooms. Restrooms are for normal use only. Do not wash dishes, hair, children or pets in the sinks.
12. One RV per site excludes tents.
13. Please notify management of any complaints at the time they occur. Six Lakes is not responsible for lost or stolen property. If campground rules are not observed, campers will be asked to leave. No refunds will be given.
14. Camping sites do not come with boat slip and all slips are reserved for paid seasonal camping.
15. No corralling, circling or horseshoeing of campers permitted.
16. Atv’s, Utv’s and Golf carts are only permitted to be used on premises by licensed seasonal tenants over 21 years of age.

The Village of Grantsburg offers two well-maintained campgrounds conveniently located along West Olson Drive, adjacent to the scenic Wood River and Memory Lake Park.
Main Campground – 300 W Olson Drive
Our primary campground features 38 full hookup sites including water, sewer, electricity, and Wi-Fi. A modern bathhouse is available for guests use. Cable TV and telephone service can be arranged through Grantsburg Telcom for an additional fee.
James N. McNally WEST – 400 W Olson Drive
Opened in September 2025, this expanded campground offers 30 diverse campsites:
7 full hookup (includes one ADA site)
7 water & electric (includes one ADA site and two pull-through sites)
5 electric only (includes two pull-through sites)
8 primitive (no services)
3 designated tent sites
A convenient on-site bathroom is available for campers.
Both campgrounds are perfect base camps for outdoor enthusiasts—whether you're here to explore Crex Meadows, enjoy fishing or hunting, or simply relax by the river.

Lake Linden Village Campground
2026 campground reservations can be made below.
CAMPGROUND RESERVATIONS
RESIDENTS AND GUESTS:
The USEPA Project in Torch Lake is scheduled to begin on the first week of June. The swimming area WILL BE CLOSED for the entire summer. The pavilion and playground adjacent to the beach, campground, and disc golf course as well as the Village Park proper (along Calumet Street) will have full access to all facilities throughout the year.
To modify or cancel reservations please call 906-369-5450 during the camping season. If no answer please leave reservation details including name, site, dates and reservation number from confirmation email.
The campground was developed in 1980 for residents and visitors to the village and surrounding Torch Lake area. The expanded campground includes 27 sites with water and electric service and rustic sites for tenting. The campground is located near the swimming area and a large open-air pavilion is available for rent or camper use if not reserved. The campground is located within walking distance of convenience stores, four restaurants, groceries, hardware store, and the Houghton County Museum which features steam engine rides throughout the summer. The adjacent Village Park has a large Tot-Lot play area, baseball field, basketball court, tennis courts, horseshoe pits, boat launch, walking trail, and an 18-hole disc golf course. The nearby Traprock River also provides excellent canoeing.
RATES: Sites with water and 30-amp electric are $32 per night , the 7th night is free. (Weekly $192)
(Not during July 4th week)
Sites with water and 50-amp electric are $35 per night and the 7th night is free. (Weekly $210) (not during July 4th week)
Rustic sites are $20 per night and the 7th night is free. (Weekly $120)

Village Services
The Village provides the following services to residents and, in the case of the water system, to those just outside the Village limits.
WATER UTILITY: The Village bills users of its water system on a bi-monthly basis on January 1st, March 1st, May 1st, July 1st, September 1st and November 1st. The following rates are effective as of March 2025:
Village resident water rate: Base: $61.00 bi-monthly Unit charge: $3.45 per 1000 gallons.
Non-resident water rate: Base: $66.00 bi-monthly Unit charge: $4.28 per 1000 gallons.
The Village also bills for the Torch Lake Area Sewage Authority (A separate entity from the Village) and that rate has a base 2-month fee of $65.08 and a per-thousand rate of $13.62, after 4000 gallons.
New homeowners or landlords bringing in new tenants should contact the Village Clerk's office at 906.296.9911 to update billing information.
GARBAGE PICK-UP: The Village collects garbage weekly on Tuesdays for residents and commercial locations within the Village only. Only garbage in color-coded Village bags, or Village dumpsters, or with a large-item sticker will be picked up. The rates and fees are as follows:
Service costs: A $50 annual fee, billed on the taxes, and a fixed millage of 1.75 mils on the property tax bills.
Garbage Bags: Small blue $5.00 roll of 10
Yellow (medium) $9.00 roll of 10
Large blue $6.00 roll of 5
Large Item stickers: $5.00 good for one item such as chair, table, stove, etc. The following exclusions apply: No refrigerators, freezers, air
conditioners, or freon appliances, tires, vehicle or marine batteries, or items containing corrosive or toxic fluids.
Items are collected on regular Tuesday collection.
Rental Dumpsters: $40.00 dumpsters are delivered on Tuesdays and collected the following Tuesday. Prohibitions are the same as for large
item stickers.
SNOW REMOVAL: The Village public works crew does provide for the opening or widening of driveways. There is a $75 fee and are as time permits for the crew after its regular snow removal operations.
SPRING AND FALL CLEAN-UPS: The Village picks up yard waste such as lawn clippings and branches that are raked out over the curbs and piled in lengths no more than 4'. There are typically three dates in the spring and three in the fall and are posted on this site and in the Daily Mining Gazette.

Why Circle “C”?
Circle “C” Campground… where a family atmosphere and non-stop fun go hand in hand.
Our natural setting, near the shores of 83-acre Bailey Pond in northeast Connecticut, presents
the perfect opportunity for your family’s outdoor enjoyment. You can launch and store your boat,
or rent one of ours, to try your luck with some of Connecticut’s finest bass fishing.
If you prefer, you can take a refreshing plunge into our clean, spring-fed swimming pond.
Organized activities for all ages abound at Circle “C”, with everything from hayrides

Rental Cabins
Circle “C” Campground has two rental cabins. The
cabins are one room rustic cabins that have wooden bunks and a
counter, and no electricity or water. These cabins sleep five and
are conveniently located near the bathrooms. The cabins are essentially
like tent camping, and for your comfort we recommend bringing air
mattresses. You must bring your linens (pillows, towels, bedding,
etc.) and anything else you may need to make your stay more comfortable.
Pets are not allowed in any of our rental cabins. There
is a two night minimum stay in all cabins.
Cabins are $50.00 per night, or $300.00 per week.
Holiday weekends are $55.00 per night.
Cabins are also subject to Connecticut tax per night.
This rate is per family unit. Only one
family is allowed per cabin, or a maximum of 4 adults. All cabins
have a fire ring and picnic table on the site. Reservation and
refund policies for cabins are the same as for regular campsites.
Please note that rental cabin check-in is 3:00 p.m. and check out

Reservation Policy
One night deposit required when making reservation. The deposit is due within 7 days by check
or if you are using a credit card, we will charge your card on the day you make your reservation.
Holiday weekends: 3 night minimum stay to be paid in full within 7 days
by check or if using a credit card the 3 nights will be charged at time of reservation.
PERSONAL CHECKS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED AT CHECK IN , cash or credit/debit only.
If you prefer to pay by check please pay in full at time of reservation.
All prices are subject to change.
While we do our best to honor requests for specific sites, we do
reserve the right to make changes when necessary.
Visitors
All rates are based on 1 Family Unit or 1 Non-Family Unit:

(Grand-children, friends, sister, brother, aunt, uncle, etc.)
Non-Family Unit: Rate is for 2 people, all others pay a guest fee if they
stay in your tent or camper. When they set up their own tent they will pay a tent site fee.

Add $3.00 to visitor rates on Holiday weekends.
Visitors checking in after 7:30 pm will be charged the overnight fee.
If you check out before the store closes you will be refunded the difference.
Overnight visitors: if you stay in the tent or camper of person you are visiting; you pay the regular guest fee. If you are putting up your own tent on the site of which you are visiting, you then pay a tent site fee.

Your Quiet Lakeside Escape in Woodstock, CT
Experience premier bass fishing, spacious RV and tent sites and peaceful nature at Chamberlain Lake
Our Campground Experience
Nestled in the "Quiet Corner" of Connecticut, Chamberlain Lake Campground offers a traditional camping experience away from the noise of the city. Whether you are pulling a big rig or pitching a tent under the pines, our family-owned campground is the perfect base for exploring Woodstock and the surrounding scenery.
Unlike crowded resorts, we prioritize peace, nature, and community. With our "no gas motors" policy on the lake, you are guaranteed a serene atmosphere perfect for kayaking, swimming, fishing and relaxing by the campfire.
Why choose us?
World-Class Bass Fishing
Cast a line into one of Connecticut's best-kept secrets. Chamberlain Lake is renowned for excellent bass fishing. Because we prohibit gas motors, the waters remain calm and the fish stay biting. No fishing license required! Bring your kayak, canoe, or electric-motor boat and enjoy the water the way nature intended. Don't have a boat or canoe? You can rent one from the camp store or through the on-line reservation system.
Big Rigs & Tents Welcome
We offer a variety of sites to match your camping style, from open family-style camping to private wooded sites.
* 30/50 Amp Service Available
* Water Hookups
* Grey Water Hookups
* Clean Dump Station & Honey Wagon Service
The Camp Store & More
Forgot the marshmallows? We’ve got you covered. Our fully stocked Camp Store carries firewood, ice, fishing supplies, and sweet and salty treats. We are dedicated to maintaining clean bathhouses and a safe, family-friendly environment where kids can ride bikes and parents can unwind.

Leave it to Bass Pro Shops to show us camping stereotypes!
Country Village Campground is a small campground with large, wooded sites located conveniently in the middle of the state with easy access to the many splendors of Vermont. A quaint village, 2 lakes, a river, a creek, restaurants, stores, entertainment and hiking trails are all within 5 miles and make activities a short walk or ride away. Saddleback Campground
Learn More
Come be part of our family at Saddleback
If peace, quiet, tranquility, rest and relaxation are what you, your family, and your friends desire when you camp, then come stay with us at Saddleback Campground in Northwood, New Hampshire. We are located within an hour to most of New Hampshire's major attractions. Or if you prefer, just stay here and "hide away from the rest of the world."
online reservation request
Please inform the office if you are planning on bringing your pet before making your reservation.
We ask that you only bring one pet, and that your pet is never left unsupervised at any time during your stay.
We also ask that visitors of registered campers do not bring their pets while visiting.
who we are
Saddleback Campground is a small, family owned & operated campground located away from the hustle and bustle of normal everyday life. From the moment you pull into our driveway, you will find our main desire is to make you feel warm and welcome, while at the same time enjoying a peaceful stay. We are conveniently located in Southern New Hampshire, within driving distance to the ocean, mountains, hiking trails, state parks or many other attractions you would like to explore.
Come and unwind
All of our camp sites have a view of our beautiful spring fed pond where you can swim or fish with no license required. Our camp sites are spacious and naturally shaded by trees. We have sites to accommodate every person's idea of camping, from tents to 50 foot motor homes. Enjoy your site or choose any of the several common areas to relax and connect with family and friends while enjoying the sounds of nature or a warm campfire.

Campground
﻿
Located in the heart of New Hampshire!
Thank you for your interest in Riverbend Campground! A place to relax, unwind and enjoy the many beautiful attractions the area has to offer. If your stay involves active days and campfire nights, Riverbend is a great place to choose as your home base. Our family purchased this beautiful campground in 2019 and we appreciate your patience as we update & GROW!.
Our goal is to create a unique and rustic camping experience for everyone to enjoy.
From "camping" to “glamping” we welcome you all!
Our small campground is conveniently located minutes from Winnipesaukee and Ossipee Lakes, as well as smaller ponds and swimming holes. Some offering boat launches, beaches & quaint
kayak/paddle board inlets.
This unique area offers everything from breweries, distilleries & creameries to live theater, farmers markets & waterfall trails. At the end of the day, return, relax & enjoy the mountain air by a crackling fire.
Call us today for site availability!

CAMPGROUND MAP
﻿
Campground policies
Safety
To ensure the safety of all our campground guests, Limit your speed to 5mph throughout the campground.
Keep an eye out for the little ones!
﻿
Visitors
There is no charge for visitors spending the day, however all visitors must check in at the office upon arrival. Guests who decide to spend the night will be charged a rate of $10. per person.
Children
Parents/guardians must be responsible for their children at all times. Children under 14 years of age are not allowed in the pool area or near the river without supervision.
Pets
We love our 4 legged family members, we have one of our own! Please keep your pet in control at all times, no excessive barking or running around off leash. A plastic bag dispenser is provided at the bath house to pick up after your pet when taking a walk.
Trash/Recycling
A dumpster is provided for camping and household trash ONLY! Absolutely no large items, electronics, grills carpets or furniture.
A dump pass is available upon request OR payment must be made for disposal. See management for info.
Quiet Hours
Please observe "quiet time" between the hours of 10pm-8am.
Keep fires small & noise levels low during these hours.
Please be respectful of your neighbors!
Payment & Refund Policy
A credit card number must be provided to hold your site. Payment in full is collected upon arrival. ﻿

Tumbling Waters Campground & Trout Pond
Small enough to be a secret, big enough that you’ll want to return!
Matthew 13:44
Campsites Fishing
Welcome
Stay at one of the oldest private campgrounds in Western North Carolina. 80 plus years of peaceful relaxation. Tucked up in a valley at 2,000 ft. above sea level you will be next to a beautiful state stock Panther Creek that falls into Lake Fontana. Catch Rainbow trout , Brook trout, and Brown trout right from your camp site. Where the star’s are bigger and brighter because you are no where near city lights. No highway noise, just creek and crickets. Hiking trails from campground.
Feel the peace of God’s great Earthly Creation as your Cares float down the creek.
Off the beaten Path, our valley is home to
Panther Creek. We can’t wait to meet you!
We are just minutes away from some of the best things to do in the smokies. Fishing, water skiing and tubing in
Lake Fontana, fast cars in Deal’s Gap and Tail of the Dragon, Whitewater rafting in the Nantahala river, The Smokey Mountain National Park, Deep creek tubing, Shopping in Bryson City, The Smokey Mountain Railroad, Joyce Kilmer Forest, Cherokee NC, Harrah’s Cherokee Casino, Tsali Mountain Bike recreational area and The Appalachian Trail.
Over the Creek Relaxation
Hang the hammock, take a nap, enjoy the sounds of nature.
Trout Fishing
Bring the kids to fish our on-site trout pond. They will surely be busy reeling them in.
Cabin Camping
Stay in one of our cozy cabins to experience the mountain cabin life.
The Chapel
Bring your faith to the creekside for our beautifully quaint bible service.
Evening Camp Fire
End each day with a warm fire and roasted marshmallows.
Front Porch Sitting
What better place to sit and rock than in the middle of the woods surrounded by the sound of nature.

Look for the Pride Swatch Mercedes onsite at Pride RV Resort and Family Campground.
RV Sites Plentiful and Pleasant
RVing in the Great Smoky Mountains just doesn’t get any better than this. The spectacular natural and man-made offerings that span North Carolina into Tennessee can be charted on any handy map—or the latest GPS device—and you’ll find Pride Resort right along your way. In fact, Maggie Valley is nature’s resting spot—the place to take a step back and look all around at the splendor of this beautiful area. We’re looking forward to your arrival. With 124 full-service pull-through RV sites, Pride Resort welcomes guests who visit in RVs of virtually any size.
All sites are level and can accommodate the big rigs.
We offer full hookups with 30 amp and 50 amp service.
Creekside sites with full hookup and with 50 amp service.
We have shaded sites or open sites.
On the creek or off the creek.
Handi-capable sites.
Picnic tables at each site.
We have oversized sites. Our largest sites are 45′.
Park Models Clean and Spacious
Not a camper? Not crazy about tenting? Pride has the perfect solution. Stay in one of our spacious park models available for rent with many of the amenities of home. Step outside—and you’re next to nature. It’s ideal. Choose from one and two-bedroom park models. Each rental is equipped with a basic set of dishes, utensils, and pots and pans. Each comes with a fully equipped kitchen. We also offer a linen service for your convenience. We have a limited number of park models available for rental, so make your plans as far in advance as possible. Each has Cable TV.
Choose from:
1 Bedroom Park Model (Queen Bed, Living Room)
2 Bedroom Park Model (Queen and Double Bed, Living Room)
Cabins Rustic and Cozy
Make your stay a rustic yet cozy getaway to remember. Rent one of our cozy cabins and cast your fishing line off your front porch—how’s that for luxury? Each has Cable TV.
Choose from:
1 Bedroom Efficiency, Sleeps Two
(Double Bed, Microwave, Stove, Small Refrigerator and Shower)
1 Bedroom Studio, Sleeps Two
(Double Bed, Love seat, Microwave, Stove, Small Refrigerator, Sink, Shower, Screened-In Porch)
TENT CAMPSITES Along Jonathan Creek
Campers looking for a tent site? We have the greatest sites in the world, and we’ve got a spot for you! Our beautiful camping sites situated along Jonathan Creek. By the creek or the fishing pond makes for an almost perfect camp site. Just add a campfire and now it is in fact, PERFECT. Showers are close by.
ASSOCIATION MEMBERS Enjoy Special Discounts:
We offer special discounts for square dancers and all our camping affiliates: Coast to Coast, AOR, RPI and Pride Members.

Explore the Great Outdoors of Franklin, North Carolina
Cullasaja River RV Park is the best place to stay for your next camping trip. The campground is located right by the river, so guests can spend the day swimming, fishing, or tubing. Regulations
For your protection, please adhere to the following rules:
A speed limit of 5 mph is strictly enforced.
Do not drive on the grass.
All campfires must be in fire rings.
Absolutely no joyriding in the park.
Only one camping unit is allowed per site.
Please respect the trees. Do not cut them, bend them, or drive nails into them.
Only one car or truck is allowed per campsite. Check our office for additional parking.
Firearms, firecrackers, fireworks, or explosives of any kind are not allowed in the camp under any circumstances.
Please keep loud and disagreeable noise to a minimum.
Quiet hour is at 10:00 PM so please remember your fellow campers. Visitors will be asked to leave the area by 11:00 PM.
Children must be supervised by an adult at all times.
Checkout time is at 12 noon. Please go to the office if you need more time.
All pets must be kept on a leash and walked in designated areas. You must also clean up after them.
Washing of vehicles is allowed by permission only.
Please help us keep restrooms clean at all times.
Please place all garbage in the dumpster.
Use the common area and your site only.
Do not walk or drive on other campsites.

These sites are right across from one of two of our bath houses.
A picnic table and fire ring is provided for you at each site.
We have 3 p/w tent sites available on the creek.
Many popup campers are small enough to fit on one of these sites. Because a converter for power will be used for a popup on these sites, they are $40 a night if booked for a popup.
Multiple tents/popup camper
Need an area for large or multiple tents or a popup/small teardrop trailer? At $40 a night for multiple tents (maximum limit of 3 tents, $20 one time fee for more than 3) and $40 a night for popups/teardrop trailers , this area has it's own shed, power/water hookup, and is located right at the bath house. (Please note the playground has been moved away from this site and is no longer at the bath house. Photos are used for an example of site size. Playground is now at the entrance of the campground.)
Multiple tents/popup camper
Sites 61B, 61C, and 62 are perfect for multiple tents! These sites are creekside, include power/water and are best suited for larger tents (10+ person tent or canopy) or a maximum limit of 3 tents per site at $40 a night ($20 one time fee for more than 3 tents). Small self contained popup or trailer will also fit on these sites for $40 a night.
please note

Our tent areas are designed for traditional camping and are not equipped for overnight stays inside vehicles. Limiting car camping also helps reduce traffic, noise, and damage to grassy areas while keeping the campground more comfortable for all guests.
If you are looking to camp in or beside your vehicle, please contact the office about alternative site options before booking.

Seasonal Sites
At this time we do not have seasonal site availability
One of the most popular questions we get asked is about availability for a permanent/seasonal site. To get straight to the point we've decided to cover all questions about seasonal sites we receive.
We have a waiting list and require everyone who is interested to fill out an application so we have your contact information and site requirements on file. Please send us an email here if interested in an application.
Once a site becomes available, we contact people on the first-come , first-served waiting list that places people in line strictly based on the order of when they applied. If that person passes on that site, we move to the next person in line.
Seasonal Site Information & Fees
Annual Lot Lease: Prices start at $1,800 per year for noncreekside and $2000 for creekside.
Electricity: Seasonal campers are responsible for paying their own monthly electric bill.
Septic & Trash Fees: An additional $200 yearly fee covers septic and trash services.
Annual Contract: All seasonal site holders must complete and sign a new contract each year, agreeing to follow all campground rules, regulations, and policies.
Our season runs from the first weekend of April until the last weekend in October.
Important Seasonal Site Policies
Rose Creek Family Campground is a place for recreation, relaxation, and enjoying the outdoors. Seasonal sites are intended for active use by campers and are not intended for storage purposes .
Seasonal campers are expected to visit and use their sites regularly throughout the camping season. Sites may not be leased solely to store an RV or camper without regular visits and recreational use.
We do not allow residential stays on campground property.
We strive to maintain a clean, safe, and welcoming environment for everyone. All seasonal campers are expected to respect campground property, fellow campers, and all established rules and policies.
About Us
We still invite you to book a stay with us!
Although we currently do not have seasonal availability, we do have sites that are open and saved for our visitors. You can view each of those sites here .

Reservations are required to access Rose Creek Family Campground. This includes camping, fishing, enjoying the creek, and using our bath houses, picnic areas, and other campground amenities.
We’re often asked about how much shade our campsites have. Our campground is surrounded by beautiful trees, but the amount of shade at any given site will vary throughout the day depending on the position of the sun. While many sites offer shade for part of the day, we cannot guarantee that a site will remain fully shaded from morning to evening.

OUTDOORS
Get Outside
Enjoy The Beautiful Outdoors in Marion County
From rock climbing to hiking and fishing, Marion County has much to offer the outdoor enthusiast!
Adventure Off Road Park
The Adventure Off Road Park, is a 500 acre tract of land located in the mountains of South Central Tennessee at 1040 Ellis Cove Road, South Pittsburg, TN 37380. The AOP is dedicated to creating the ultimate off road experience for off roaders and outdoor enthusiasts. There are over 120+ Trails in the park that offer a wide variety of difficult levels for any off road vehicle. They have plenty of camping green space at the park.
For more information visit Adventure Off Road Park .
Canoe Kayak Chattanooga
Canoe Kayak Chattanooga offers $35 all day kayak rentals, and drop offs are available at three miles, eight miles, and 13 miles. Additionally, pontoon and lund fishing boats are available to rent.
Located in Whitwell, Canoe Kayak Chattanooga is on 13 private, flat acres of an island in the middle of the 27 mile long Tennessee River Gorge.
For more information, visit Canoe Kayak Chattanooga .
Denny Cove
Denny Cove in Marion County is part of South Cumberland State Park. The beautiful natural area offers rock climbing, hiking, scenic views and a gorgeous waterfall, Denny Falls. The rock climbing organizations, Southeastern Climbers Coalition and The Access Fund, worked alongside The Conservation Fund and Land Trust for Tennessee for almost five years to acquire Denny Cove. Denny Cove offers approximately 150 climbing routes. The unique sandstone offers routes of all grades and ability levels and boasts a wide variety of terrain—from long overhanging walls to massive roofs, slabs, cracks, and corners. Please read the usage details here when planning your trip to Denny Cove .
Foster Falls - TVA Small Wild Area
Foster Falls Small Wild Area (SWA) located in Marion County, consists of approximately 178 acres. It is a focal point and a drawing card for thousands of outdoor enthusiasts that seek recreational opportunities in the South Cumberland State Recreation area. Activities include rock climbing, hiking and camping.
TVA provides picnic facilities and a campground for overnight visitors. Facilities include restrooms, a picnic pavilion managed by the TVA resident manager, a handicap accessible boardwalk, viewing platform and a wooded picnic area. Learn more about Foster Falls .
Hales Bar Marina and Resort
Hales Bar Marina and Resort rests in a stunning seventy-four (74) acre park. It is a full-service marina and RV/cabin resort by the beautiful Nickajack Lake located at 1265 Hales Bar Road, Guild, Tennessee, 37340 at mile marker 431.1L.
For more information and a full list of services offered, visit Hales Bar Marina .
Little Cedar Mountain Small Wild Area Trail
Little Cedar Mountain Trail is located about 3 miles northwest of Nickajack Dam. One of the few TVA trails that is rated difficult because of steep climbs and trail length. But don’t let that stop you, because the view from the overlook is well worth the trek. There is a vernal pond there, meaning that the pond goes dry and it does not support fish. It does support some amphibians though, so expect to see frogs and salamanders. Along the way, you can see an old stone wall that at one time stretched several miles along the shoreline.
The Little Cedar Mountain (LCM) trail is 3 mile loop with a connecting pond trail that is 1 mile long.
Photo by Tracy Burroughs Brown
Marion County Park
Located in the Nickajack Reservoir at 9696 Highway 41, Jasper, Tennessee 37347. This campground is perfect for families! The campground includes tent and RV sites, a boat ramp and recreational activities such as swimming, boating and fishing. The park includes pavilions and a stage that can be reserved and rented (pavilion and stage rental are free to Marion County residents). For more information, please call 423 942 6653 .
Prentice Cooper State Forest and Wildlife area
Nearly 26,000 acres of protected forest in Marion County are available to the public for activities such as hiking, camping, rock climbing, horseback riding, hunting and fishing. The area is open daily during daylight hours, sunrise to sunset. Learn more about visiting Prentice Cooper .
Photo by Liz A. Sexton
Sasquatch Farm RV Park
Located on South Pittsburg Mountain, Sasquatch Farm RV Park features 54 full hook-up RV spots, various primitive tent camping spots, as well as several amenities. Sasquatch Farm offers a well-stocked camp store, propane for sale, bathroom and shower facilities, free laundry facilities for guests staying on property, 130 acres of property to explore, over five miles of hiking and mountain bike trails, several waterfalls, a cave, as well as two lakes with fishing, canoeing, and paddle boards. Learn more at SasquatchFarm.com .
Sequatchie Cave Class II Natural-Scientific State Natural Area
"Sequatchie Cave Natural Area is home to two aquatic species found exclusively at this location and one other within the Sequatchie Valley: the Royal Snail and the rare Sequatchie Caddisfly." – Jenni Frankenberg Veal
For more information visit Sequatchie Cave State Natural Area or call the Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) at 615 532 0431.
Sequatchie Cove Farm
Sequatchie Cove Farm is a diversified farm of 300 acres nestled in the shadows of the Cumberland Plateau, located 35 minutes northwest of downtown Chattanooga. The farm is bordered by the Little Sequatchie River and is surrounded by thousands of acres of pristine Tennessee wilderness. The farm is run by Bill and Miriam Keener, Kelsey and Ashley Keener, Miriam’s parents Jim and Emily Wright, and an assortment of seasonal helpers from our community and beyond. Learn more about Sequatchie Cove Farm .
Sequatchie Valley Scenic Bikeways
With stunning mountain backdrop scenery, miles of low-traffic farm roads, and an abundance of historic landmarks, the Sequatchie Valley is the perfect playground for cycling adventures! Each of the Scenic Bikeway routes have been carefully mapped to maximize your time on the bike, giving you the best scenery, the most enjoyable roads, and the most interesting landmarks. To that end, each map highlights "points of interest" along the way - restaurants, rest stops, historic landmarks, etc.
For more information, including maps, visit Sequatchie Valley Scenic Bikeways .
Sweetens Cove Golf Club
Sweetens Cove Golf Club, the hand-crafted masterpiece by King-Collins Golf Course Design, is considered by multiple architecture critics as being the best nine-hole golf course in the United States. In addition, Sweetens Cove received the highest average rating of ALL golf courses in Tennessee, Alabama, Mississippi and Louisiana in The Confidential Guide to Golf Courses, v. 2 .
"I have never had more people tell me to play a course than Sweetens Cove in South Pittsburg, Tennessee. Once you begin your round, you find course conditions that would rival many of the top courses in the country. The massive undulating greens are smooth as glass and very firm. The fairways are fast and cut tight, similar to what you’d find in the UK and the bunkers are all in excellent shape. After a few holes you realize the caliber of championship golf and think, 'I’ve got to tell everyone about this…' At that point you’ve accidentally joined the Sweetens Cove cult." – Graylyn Loomis, Assistant Editor, Links Magazine
For more information, visit Sweetens Cove Golf Club .
Tennessee River Gorge Island Cabins and Tennessee River Gorge Mountain Cabins
The Tennessee River Gorge Island Cabins are private waterfront cabins on five acres of the Tennessee River Gorge Island. There are currently three cabins available to rent on the island.
On the mountain, there are two Tennessee River Gorge Mountain Cabins currently available and four more coming soon. The mountain cabins are Amish-built and are located in a 12-acre mountain forest.
Each cabin is private, located where you cannot see or hear the other properties. The cabins are available at different prices and offer different amenities. Booking any of these properties includes a covered deck, outdoor dining space, shared swimming pool, A/C, boat docks, one canoe or two kayaks, a gas grill, and one crate of firewood.
For more information, visit Tennessee River Gorge .
Trails Training Center (TTC)
The Trails Training Center is an all-inclusive motorcycle resort located at 300 Woodland Road, Sequatchie, TN 37374. TTC offers a great motorcycle vacation and includes on-site camping, classes with rental bikes and experienced, expert, patient riding instructors.
For more information, visit Trial Training Center .

SERVICES
Find the Right Department
Service Areas
Marion County Administrator of Elections
The Marion County Election Commission, often referred to as MCEC, is responsible for registering a person to vote; replace lost registration cards, and the transfer or change of registrations. It is the mission of the MCEC to provide federal, state, and local election products to eligible citizens of Marion County so they have equal access to the election process and can exercise their right to vote. The MCEC also qualifies a person to run for election to an office, and is responsible for purging or removing a person from the permanent registration records.
For more information, please visit their website at: www.marionvotes.com
You may register to vote online at: ovr.govote.tn.gov
Marion County Administrator of Elections, Tina Worstrom - 423 942 2108
Marion County Assessor of Property
The Marion County Assessor of Property office can help you with questions regarding property valuations and assessment, property address updates, GIS (Geographic Information System) mapping for taxation purposes. The Assessor's office is responsible for setting the appraised value for each parcel of land and any improvements on the land.
Marion County Assessor of Property, Darrell Pittman - 423 942 3494
Marion County Building and Planning Office
The office provides permitting for unincorporated areas of Marion County, Tennessee. Permitting for property located in any of Marion County’s cities is through that city.
The Building Office issues building permits for commercial, residential, storage, pole barns, mechanical, plumbing, decks, in ground pools, cell towers, roof mounted solar panels and mobile homes. The Building Official performs Footing, Foundation, Framing, Mechanical, Plumbing and Final Building Inspections. The Building Official is also the FEMA (Flood Administrator) for unincorporated Marion County, Tennessee.
The Planning Office provides administrative support for subdivisions of property, plat submissions and coordination of Final Plat recording. They also provide administrative support to the Marion County Regional Planning Commission.
Marion County Building Official, Gabe Yeargan - 423 942 8019
Administrative Staff, Tammy McDulin - 423 942 3527
Administrative Staff, Renea Wilson - 423 942 3527
For additional information, visit:
https://marioncountytn.net/planning-building
Marion County Circuit Court Clerk
General Sessions and Circuit Courts are responsible for Tennessee Highway Patrol citations, county citations, misdemeanor and felony criminal charges, and all paperwork and cost associated with each case. Civil accounts are managed in both courts. General Sessions administers recovery warrants, detainers, debit, writs and garnishments, order of protection and judicial committals. Circuit Court administers divorces, child support, adoptions, worker's compensation, damages auto and non-auto, foreign judgement, breach of contract, wrongful death, malpractice, condemnation, contempt, name change, minor settlements, forfeitures, hospital liens, legitimation and appeals to the court of appeals. Circuit court is also responsible for managing jurors for Grand Jury and jury trials.
Marion County Circuit Court Clerk, Lonna Henderson - 423 942 2134
Marion County Clerk
Registration of new vehicles, collecting all taxes; Renewals; Duplicate titles; Placards; Business license; Registration of boats, collecting all taxes; Manufactured Home permits; Beer applications; Beer taxes; Marriages and certified marriage copies; Notary certification and notary renewals; Organ Donor collections; Record Dealer license; Collect Juvenile fines and restitution; Monitor Trust funds; Record the County Commission meeting minutes.
The Marion County Clerk's office has applications for premarital pre-course, Beer, New Business, Notary, disability plates/placards, and personalized plates.
This office provides online service for Renewals at www.tntagsanytime.com .
Our methods of payment are cash, check, and credit or debit card. Please be aware there is a fee charged by the payment clearing house for processing card payments which is a 2% fee of your total payment.
Marion County Clerk, Joanie Spangler - 423 942 2515
Marion County Clerk and Master
The Chancery Court handles cases involving domestic relations, worker's compensation, estates, trusts, contracts, collect delinquent taxes, guardianships, and conservatorships, dissolution of partnerships and corporations, enforcement of liens, boundary lines, breach of contract, fraud, election contests and other matters of a civil nature. The Clerk and Master handles the paperwork and fees associated with this court, and is sometimes called upon to act as a Chancellor to the court.
Marion Clerk and Master, Paige Mashburn - 423 942 2601
Marion County EMA (Emergency Management Agency)
It is our goal to achieve both daily and during times of emergencies the highest level of service for our customers, the public. We reach this goal by identifying, preparing, and responding to any need the public has. As individuals we will prepare to meet these challenges through training and vigilance, always recognizing the need to conduct ourselves in a professional manner with both our peers and the public.
Notification System Sign-Up Instructions
Website: https://www.tnmcema.org/
Marion County EMA Director: Steve Lamb- (423)-942-2528

The Register of Deeds office is the established custodian and land library for all real estate transactions within Marion County. Marion County Road Superintendent
The Marion County Highway Department is committed to the maintenance of county roads, right of ways, and bridges that are deemed part of the county road system, as approved by the County Commission.
Marion County Road Superintendent, Cory Pickett - 423 942 2581
This office is closed on Friday
Marion County Soil and Water Conservation District
The Marion County Soil and Water Conservation District works with landowners to help reduce soil erosion, protect water quality, improve grazing land and wildlife habitat. This office provides information on installing and implementing such conservation practices as crop land conversion, composting and litter storage facilities, fencing cattle out of rivers and streams and providing alternative watering systems.
For additional information, visit their website at http://marionscd.com .
District Conservationist, Cody Brown: 423 371 1286 or cody.brown2@usda.gov
Office Manager, Debbie Smith: 423 942 2244 ext. 3 or Deborah.Smith@tn.nacdnet.net
Natural Resource Specialist, Betsy Bowden: 423 651 3005 tipton.bowden@usda.gov
Marion County Trustee
The Trustee's office acts as a treasurer for the county and serves two primary functions: 1) collecting all county property taxes; and 2) keeping a regular accounting of all money received.
Property Tax Payment Options: 1) In the Trustee's office; 2) by mail; 3) online at www.tennesseetrustee.com. From this site, you can also check to see if your mortgage company has paid your property taxes and find other helpful property tax information.
Property Tax Methods of Payment: 1) Cash; 2) check; 3) credit or debit card. If using a credit or debit card, please be aware there is a fee charged by the payment clearing house for processing card payments which is 2.75% of the total amount you owe.
Property Tax Relief: The Trustee administers a state funded program for qualifying citizens who are 1) 65 years of age or older; 2) 100% disabled or 3) 100% disabled veteran (service connected). Applications for tax relief must be filled out in the Trustees office.
Marion County Trustee, Connie Schaerer - 423 942 2681

This office provides services to local veterans. Hours of operation are Tuesday-Thursday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

River Fun & Camping in the Pristine Toccoa Valley
Fresh Air Family Fun in Blue Ridge, Georgia
Nestled in the unspoiled Chatahoochee-Oconee National Forest of the Blue Ridge Mountains of Georgia, Toccoa Valley Campground hosts thousands of local and international visitors annually for both river running and camping adventures. Whether you want to float or paddle your way beside the generous green overhang of old-growth trees or pitch your tent on the gently winding banks for some fishing and R&R, Toccoa Valley Campground delivers the best in fresh-air family fun.
Get Directions
Tubing, Rafting & Kayaking
~~~~~~~~~~
Experience the beautiful Toccoa River through miles of protected national forest on a tube.
River Fun Opens in May!
Looking to raft or kayak? No need to make reservations! Rafters and kayakers are served on a first come first serve basis.
Book Tubing Trip
Toccoa Valley Camping
~~~~~~~~~~
Spend some nights under the Blue Ridge mountain stars on the shore of the Toccoa River at TVC’s well-managed campground
featuring complete RV hookups for power and plumbing
Book RV Camping
Book Tent Camping
Why Toccoa Valley Campground?
~~~~~~~~~~
Safety
As a family-owned business, we’re dedicated to providing a safe, fun-filled experience for all ages! With ten acres of private land, we offer dedicated parking, where families can gather without having to cross or walk alongside the roadway. Before you hit the water, our staff will provide thorough briefings to make sure everyone is safely equipped, and our entry and exit ramps make getting in and out of the river simple and easy.
Clean and Uncrowded Facilities
We strive to always provide clean facilities and accommodations for our guests. Between our tidy bathrooms and private changing rooms, you’ll have everything you need to feel at home. Even on our busiest days, our spacious grounds and river access are managed to ensure the experience never feels crowded. You came here to escape the masses and we want to make sure it stays that way.
Best Float on the Toccoa!
Experience Georgia’s original tubing destination! Family-owned for four generations, Toccoa Valley Campground offers the longest tubing trip in the area. At over four miles long, our route carries you through the untouched beauty of the national forest. It’s a one-of-a-kind journey you won’t want to miss!
Little to No Wait Time
Nothing slows you down at Toccoa Valley Campground! Once you’ve grabbed your gear and had a quick safety briefing, you’re free to hit the water, no reservations or wait times required. When your float is finished, forget the long trek back; our continuous shuttle service takes you back to your vehicle, where your dry clothes are waiting.
No Reservations Or Wait Times For Tubing
Free Parking & Complimentary Shuttle
Free Life Jackets Provided for Everyone
Clean Restrooms and Changing Rooms
Convenience Store for Snacks & Supplies!
The Original Toccoa River Experience
In the 1960s, visionary TVC founder Herman Long began inviting passing travelers to unwind on his beautiful acres on the Toccoa River. Back then, it was truck tires for tubes and no public restrooms, but the combination of natural beauty and family welcome still made it all worth while.
Four generations later, Herman’s descendants still run Toccoa Valley Campground the way their grandfather did. Sure, the tubes have been upgraded to our signature pink and our clean and plumbed restroom facilities make our competitors’ porta-Johns look primitive, but, the land remains virtually the same as Herman left it, and Toccoa Valley Campground, already the oldest tubing operation in all of Georgia, continues to make a reasonable claim to being the best as well.
Our History
From Long’s family to yours, we invite you to share in the pristine beauty of the Toccoa River as it was always meant to be experienced.
Ray & Gina Golden • Owners
Frequently Asked Questions
~~~~~~~~~~
May I bring alcohol?
No. Alcohol is strictly prohibited on all TVC property, both on our campgrounds and on the river.
How old does someone need to be to ride down the river?
We recommend that children be five or older to ride the river with a life jacket. Life jackets are provided for every rider, and are required for every rider 12 years old and younger.
May I bring my own tube?
Yes, you may bring your own tube. We will still provide a shuttle back from our disembark point after you reach it.
May I bring a cooler on the river, even without alcohol?
No. Coolers may not be taken on the river, as this poses a hazard. Exceptions can be made for medical purposes. Water bottles and other non-alcoholic drinks may be carried. Speak to our staff if you have a question.

Electricity
30-amp electrical power is available at every RV site.
Full Service Bathrooms and Showers

Tents are not allowed on RV camping sites.

We now have locations in SW Columbus off of Hwy 45 ALT near the GTR Airport, Weyerhaeuser, The Industrial Park, Paccar, & Steel Dynamics and also off of Military Road in North Columbus near Lion Hills Golf Course. We are conveniently located near Mississippi State and EMCC.
Hidden Cove was built in the 60's by the Mullin and Swartz families and friends, originally for private use. They enjoyed many years of camping and camaraderie, eventually building a lodge on the property used for group dinners, club meetings, card playing etc. Lots of fun and laughs. Electrical wires ran through the trees like spiderwebs, all of that is underground now. The lodge is still there in it's original condition, no longer in use but part of the landscape nonetheless. It was built from heart pine and whatever brick and tin they could get their hands on at the time, complete with a 5 ft. fireplace with pot hangers. There's a handmade wood mantle with signatures. Maybe one day it will be restored for use. When it was purchased by our family in the 80's that was our intention and we did use it for many years for family gatherings, Easter Egg Hunts, parties, dinners etc. We would sometimes "float the river" and then meet back at the lodge for a meal afterwards. Fun times.
We are not a resort, just a small family and friend kind of campground. We like to maintain a clean and safe environment for camping. We hope you feel that here too.

RVs & Camping on the Mulberry River
Experience the best tent and RV camping in Arkansas at Byrd’s Adventure Center. Right on the Mulberry River , Byrd’s offers a host of activities not found at any other Ozark campground.
Enjoy our comfortable RV and tent campsites as you relax in the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas. Byrd’s Adventure Center offers spacious camping in a beautiful setting along the Mulberry River.
A variety of grassy and wooded campsites are available. Some sites have small shelters with picnic tables and campfire rings. In addition to our new Riverfront Restaurant (open weekly Friday-Sunday), we have more amenities than you’ll find in other Ozark campgrounds. These include a large heated shower house, a convenient on-site store with deli, stages, pavilions, an extensive trail network , two backcountry airstrips, rental cabins , plus floating and fishing on the pristine Mulberry River. All of this is located on our private 800-acre ORV park surrounded by the Ozark National Forest.
You’ll enjoy access to the wild and scenic Mulberry River , trails in the Ozark National Forest, our large heated shower house, aircraft runways , and the great ATV, UTV and 4×4 trails that Byrd’s Adventure Center is famous for.

FEES SUBJECT TO CHANGE WITHOUT NOTICE
Cancellation Policy
All reservations pay a 25% nonrefundable deposit at the time of booking. The remainder of your balance is due upon check-in.
Cancellations made less than 30 days before your check-in date will be charged 50% of the stay.
Cancellations made 14 days or less before your check-in date will be charged for 100% of the stay.
Camping fun continues rain or shine. We do not allow cancellations due to weather, unless there is imminent flooding.
Byrd’s Campground Rules & Regulations
1. Anyone entering Byrd’s Adventure Center must sign the Waiver and Release of Liability Form. Minors must be signed in by parents.
2. If you arrive after office hours you will not be permitted on the trails until you sign the waiver the next morning. The store opens at 9 am.
3. During events, all spectators must stay in designated areas. No exceptions.
4. No firearms, fireworks or explosives allowed.
5. Do not litter. Anyone caught littering will be asked to leave. Place your trash in one of the dumpsters before you leave, or “Pack It In, Pack It Out”. You can recycle aluminum cans by bringing them to the store.
6. TREAD LIGHTLY. Keep your speed low, 5mph maximum, while entering or exiting the park. Stay on designated roads or trails only. Staff off the grass. No spin outs, donuts, wheelies or other reckless driving will be tolerated. You will be asked to leave.
7. Do not remove or destroy trees, shrubs, plants or animals.
8. Absolutely no digging, trenching or altering the grounds of the park. No exceptions. Fines may apply.
9. All pets must be on a leash.
10. Do not gather or cut firewood on the property. It is for sale at the store.
11. Do not build new fire pits. Keep fires contained in existing fire pits. Do not put trash or glass in fire pits. If you need a fire pit at your campsite, check with the store to see if it is possible.
12. Be courteous of other campers and Park Employees at all times.
13. Do not pull down on the bank of the river or in the river with any vehicle.
14. Do not remove or mess with any caution tape, trail markers, or signs of any kind.
15. Failure to comply with the above rules and regulations may result in your being temporarily or permanently banned from using the park or participating in any future park activity or event. No refund of any monies will be given.
16. The park is neither liable or responsible for damage, loss, or theft of personal property or injury to visitors.
17. All pets must be on a leash.
18. No hunting allowed.
19. This is a family-oriented campground. We will not tolerate any fighting, underage drinking, nudity, loud profane language, loud music, or any general drunken misbehavior.

Mulberry Mountain RV & Tent Campground
OPEN YEAR ROUND!
Enjoy beautiful wooded sites at this incredible campground in the Arkansas Ozarks Mountains. Features include convenient pull through sites with water and electric hook-ups (50 amp, 30 amp, & 110v hookups at each site), numerous primitive campsites, large shade trees throughout, nice clean bathroom/shower house, easy access septic disposal, and much more.
Miles and miles of ATV, hiking, biking and horse trails can be easily accessed directly from the Mulberry Mountain campground. Four large fishing ponds are located on the property. Mulberry Mountain also just a short drive from the National Scenic Mulberry River for swimming, fishing, floating, and more. Call us today and start planning your next vacation at Mulberry Mountain!

ATV Trails, Hiking Trails (waterfalls & more), Biking Trails, Horse Trails, Scenery & Wildlife, Mulberry River (swimming, fishing, canoeing), Fishing Ponds, Hunting, Scenic Byways, Winery Tours (Altus, AR), and more!

Feel the Rush of Arkansas Outdoors
From first-time adventurers to seasoned thrill-seekers, Arkansas offers outdoor challenges that are exciting, accessible and unforgettable.
Arkansas is made for adventure, with landscapes that invite you to test your limits or just try something new. In the Ozark and Ouachita Mountains, the Monument Trails at Mount Nebo and Devil’s Den state parks take bikers along ridgelines, through winding switchbacks and down fast, flowy descents. Gravel riders trade mountain views for wide-open stretches on the Delta Heritage Trail, while climbers head to Petit Jean State Park, Horseshoe Canyon Ranch , Sam’s Throne and Mount Magazine to grip sandstone walls and earn big sky views.
If speed is your thrill, the Wolf Pen Gap Trail System in Mena offers 40 miles of rugged ATV tracks through the pines. Racetracks across the state keep hearts pounding with drag racing, dirt ovals and motorcycle runs. For the ultimate rush, leap from a plane on a tandem skydive or launch a hang glider from Mount Magazine and watch valleys unfold beneath your feet.
Water brings its own excitement. The Cossatot River turns wild with Class IV–V rapids after heavy rains, while the Spring River flows cold and clear all year, perfect for rafting or kayaking.
Families can find their own adrenaline high on zip line courses in Hot Springs , Ponca and Eureka Springs , where canopy tours mix fast cables with rope bridges and forest views.
Whether it’s your first time on a trail or your hundredth day on the water, Arkansas makes it easy to dive in. Outfitters and guides are ready to help beginners gear up, while seasoned adventurers will discover challenges worth bragging about. From mountaintop to riverbank, Arkansas is the place to feel the rush of the outdoors.

Welcome to Arkansas
Arkansas is a state of six distinct regions. Every corner of The Natural State has its own character and story, from the rolling hills and clear rivers of the Ozarks to the rich cultural heritage of the Delta. Central Arkansas adds lakes and city energy, while the Ouachita Mountains deliver scenic drives, forested peaks and inviting thermal springs. The River Valley offers expansive views from its mountaintops to the shores of the Arkansas River, while the Timberlands pair towering pines with oil-boom history and presidential roots.
Select a region to see more
The Ozarks
Arkansas’ Wild Side Shines in the Ozarks
Nature worked wonders in the Ozark Mountains, carving a landscape of soaring bluffs, hidden caverns, wooded valleys and rolling ridgelines that now set the stage for some of Arkansas' most exciting outdoor adventures. Lakes, rivers and the legendary fly fishing waters of the White and Little Red draw anglers and paddlers from across the country. More than 40 miles of the Razorback Greenway link parks, downtowns, breweries, art museums, live music and eateries. Spend a day here with a casual bike ride from a hotel to a James Beard-nominated restaurant, then world-class mountain biking on OZ Trails. Watching the sun rise from a cabin overlooking the Buffalo National River, then fade to dusk as elk bugle in nearby fields. Exploring Blanchard Springs Caverns by day and listening to live music on an Ozark town square at night. From college towns to lake towns to river towns, the Ozarks prove that urban energy and outdoor culture share the same stage.
Explore this region
: The Ozarks
The Timberlands
From Pine Forests to Presidential Roots
From the pine forests of El Dorado to the historic streets of Hope and Camden, the Timberlands region tells Arkansas stories in bold ways. Walk through Smackover’s Arkansas Museum of Natural Resources to learn how the oil boom transformed the state, then step into El Dorado’s lively downtown, where historic buildings now house shops and restaurants. History buffs can head to Historic Washington State Park to see where a Bowie knife was first forged, or tour President Bill Clinton’s boyhood home in Hope.
Explore this region
: The Timberlands
The Delta
Where Blues, Barbecue and History Run Deep
The Arkansas Delta stretches along the Mississippi River, where farmland, river towns and outdoor traditions define the region. Waterfowlers come for renowned duck hunting, while Crowley’s Ridge adds scenic overlooks and hiking trails that break up the flat landscape. In Helena, the Delta Cultural Center broadcasts King Biscuit Time, and each October the King Biscuit Blues Festival draws music lovers from across the country. From riverfront stops to Marianna’s James Beard-recognized Jones Bar-B-Q Diner, the Delta pairs blues, barbecue and outdoor recreation in one distinctive corner of Arkansas.
Explore this region
: The Delta
Capital
The Heart of The Natural State
The Capital Region of Arkansas shows off the full Arkansas experience with the rich culture of the state’s capital city surrounded by natural beauty. Packed with arts, dining, breweries, distilleries and entertainment venues, both Little Rock and North Little Rock have walkable downtowns with access to riverfront trails for hiking and biking. The Big Dam Bridge, built for walkers and cyclists, spans the Arkansas River and links the cities. The surrounding landscape shifts from river bottoms to forested ridges within minutes, leading to adventure at places like Pinnacle Mountain State Park. Farther out, paddlers find calm water on the Saline River and Lake Maumelle, while anglers chase bass along shaded banks. College-town Conway adds boutiques and cafes, while tiny Scott surprises with a prehistoric mound site. Here, city life and outdoor fun sit closer together than you'd expect.
Explore this region
: Capital
River Valley
Mountains Above, Rivers Below
In the Arkansas River Valley, flat-topped mountains, rivers and wineries invite exploration. At Petit Jean State Park, you can climb sandstone formations on the Seven Hollows Trail or step into Rock House Cave to see prehistoric rock art. Mount Nebo State Park has become a bucket-list destination for mountain bikers on the Monument Trails, while Mount Magazine State Park stands as the state’s highest point with views that stretch for miles. Fish the Arkansas River, camp and swim at Blue Mountain Lake or tour a winery. The River Valley is made for adventure.
Explore this region
: River Valley
The Ouachitas
Ancient Mountains, Modern Adventures
The Ouachita Mountains deliver some of Arkansas’ most varied adventures, from thru-hiking the 223-mile Ouachita National Recreation Trail to soaking in the thermal waters of Hot Springs National Park. Camping, paddling, boating, mountain biking and fishing all thrive here. Lake Ouachita, one of the cleanest lakes in the country, anchors the region's water recreation. Between crystal digging near Mount Ida, mountain drives on the Talimena National Scenic Byway, and spa time in Hot Springs, the Ouachitas balance outdoor adventure with restoration.

Find Your Perfect Campsite in The Natural State
Experience the best of Arkansas camping, from mountaintop views to lakeside retreats made for tents, campers and RVs.
Arkansas is a camper’s paradise offering everything from secluded backcountry sites to family-friendly campgrounds with full hookups. Pitch a tent beneath the pines at Shores Lake in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest, settle in at the RV park at the Mena / Ouachita National Forest KOA Journey or relax lakeside at Bull Shoals-White River State Park. For something quieter, set up camp at the Wolf Pen Recreation Area near Cass or along the Cossatot River’s clear banks. With options spread across every region you can find your ideal base for hiking, paddling or simply soaking in the views.
Arkansas campgrounds range from primitive forest sites to modern parks with electricity, hot showers and picnic areas, many welcoming pets too. Spend your days fishing at DeGray Lake, floating the Buffalo National River or exploring the trails near Lake Sylvia Recreation Area. Whether you’re road-tripping in your RV, backpacking under the stars or planning a long weekend in nature, camping in Arkansas offers the perfect mix of comfort, scenery and adventure.

Bike, Hike and Camp in Arkansas’ Coler Mountain Bike Preserve
Want a utopian experience? Head to Coler Mountain Bike Preserve in Bentonville, Arkansas. While it is a mountain bikers paradise in Northwest Arkansas, anyone who enjoys a stroll in the great outdoors will love it too. If you also like camping, coffee and outdoor beer gardens, you’re really in for a treat.

Pitch Your Tent. Park Your RV. Camp Under the Arkansas Stars.
Arkansas’ state park campgrounds make it easy to connect with nature. With 32 parks offering campsites, you’ll find the perfect spot for quiet mornings, starry skies and fresh air.
Camping in an Arkansas State Park brings you closer to the state’s most breathtaking landscapes. Watch the sunrise over the cliffs at Petit Jean State Park, hike through hardwood forests at Devil’s Den or fall asleep beside the quiet waters of Lake Ouachita. From the peaks of Mount Magazine to the clear streams of the Ozark National Forest, every park offers its own mix of scenery, recreation and relaxation.
Arkansas State Parks feature more than 2,000 campsites ranging from primitive tent areas to full-service RV pads with water, electric and sewer hookups. Many parks, like DeGray Lake Resort and Lake Catherine, offer lakeside camping with swimming and boating access, while Mount Nebo and Woolly Hollow provide scenic overlooks and shaded forest sites. Campgrounds include clean restrooms, hot showers, picnic tables and fire rings. Group camping areas are available at select parks, and most locations are pet-friendly. Browse the parks below to find your campsite and start planning your next Arkansas camping adventure.

Unique Stays You’ll Only Find in Arkansas State Parks
Looking for something a little different? Arkansas’ state parks offer unique ways to stay, from round-walled yurts and cozy camper cabins to scenic horse camps and a historic jailhouse bed and breakfast.
Arkansas State Parks offer more than traditional cabins and campgrounds. From round-walled yurts and cozy camper cabins to rental RVs and horse camps, each stay adds something special to your park experience. Rent-A-YURT guests enjoy electricity, wood floors and screened windows, while Rent-An-RV locations offer air conditioning, private bathrooms and outdoor decks with grills. Camper Cabins provide beds, screened porches and picnic areas for a comfortable outdoor retreat.
For something truly one of a kind, spend the night at the restored Jailhouse Bed and Breakfast in Historic Washington State Park. Equestrians can set up at horse camps with stalls, wash bays and easy trail access at select parks. Whether you’re after rustic charm, unique history or an adventure that feels completely new, these stays offer unforgettable ways to experience The Natural State.

Experience the best of Arkansas camping, from mountaintop views to lakeside retreats made for tents, campers and RVs.
Arkansas is a camper’s paradise offering everything from secluded backcountry sites to family-friendly campgrounds with full hookups. Pitch a tent beneath the pines at Shores Lake in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest, settle in at the RV park at the Mena / Ouachita National Forest KOA Journey or relax lakeside at Bull Shoals-White River State Park. For something quieter, set up camp at the Wolf Pen Recreation Area near Cass or along the Cossatot River’s clear banks. With options spread across every region you can find your ideal base for hiking, paddling or simply soaking in the views.
Arkansas campgrounds range from primitive forest sites to modern parks with electricity, hot showers and picnic areas, many welcoming pets too. Spend your days fishing at DeGray Lake, floating the Buffalo National River or exploring the trails near Lake Sylvia Recreation Area. Whether you’re road-tripping in your RV, backpacking under the stars or planning a long weekend in nature, camping in Arkansas offers the perfect mix of comfort, scenery and adventure.

If you also like camping, coffee and outdoor beer gardens, you’re really in for a treat.

Pitch Your Tent. Park Your RV. Camp Under the Arkansas Stars.
Arkansas’ state park campgrounds make it easy to connect with nature. With 32 parks offering campsites, you’ll find the perfect spot for quiet mornings, starry skies and fresh air.
Camping in an Arkansas State Park brings you closer to the state’s most breathtaking landscapes. Watch the sunrise over the cliffs at Petit Jean State Park, hike through hardwood forests at Devil’s Den or fall asleep beside the quiet waters of Lake Ouachita. From the peaks of Mount Magazine to the clear streams of the Ozark National Forest, every park offers its own mix of scenery, recreation and relaxation.
Arkansas State Parks feature more than 2,000 campsites ranging from primitive tent areas to full-service RV pads with water, electric and sewer hookups. Many parks, like DeGray Lake Resort and Lake Catherine, offer lakeside camping with swimming and boating access, while Mount Nebo and Woolly Hollow provide scenic overlooks and shaded forest sites. Campgrounds include clean restrooms, hot showers, picnic tables and fire rings. Group camping areas are available at select parks, and most locations are pet-friendly. Browse the parks below to find your campsite and start planning your next Arkansas camping adventure.

Unique Stays You’ll Only Find in Arkansas State Parks
Looking for something a little different? Arkansas’ state parks offer unique ways to stay, from round-walled yurts and cozy camper cabins to scenic horse camps and a historic jailhouse bed and breakfast.
Arkansas State Parks offer more than traditional cabins and campgrounds. From round-walled yurts and cozy camper cabins to rental RVs and horse camps, each stay adds something special to your park experience. Rent-A-YURT guests enjoy electricity, wood floors and screened windows, while Rent-An-RV locations offer air conditioning, private bathrooms and outdoor decks with grills. Camper Cabins provide beds, screened porches and picnic areas for a comfortable outdoor retreat.
For something truly one of a kind, spend the night at the restored Jailhouse Bed and Breakfast in Historic Washington State Park. Equestrians can set up at horse camps with stalls, wash bays and easy trail access at select parks. Whether you’re after rustic charm, unique history or an adventure that feels completely new, these stays offer unforgettable ways to experience The Natural State.
