Benefits of Long-term RV Parks
Why It’s the Smart Choice for Campers
Long-term camping offers the perfect balance of adventure and relaxation. Save money and headaches, build community, explore deeper, and spend more time enjoying the outdoors.
Book Your Long-term Spot
1. Significant Cost Savings
One of the most obvious advantages of a monthly reservation is the cost. Campgrounds typically offer reduced rates for extended stays, and the savings can be substantial when compared to daily or weekly fees.
Example: If a campground charges $75 per night, a week costs $525. However, a monthly rate is $650–$800/mo with utilities and Wi-Fi included. That’s a 40% discount over nightly rates.
2. Less Hassle, More Stability
When you reserve nightly or weekly, you may find yourself packing up and moving frequently, even when you'd rather stay put. Campsites can book up quickly—especially during peak seasons—making it hard to secure a good spot without constant planning.
A monthly reservation offers peace of mind. Once you’re set up, you can settle in without the stress of moving or constantly checking availability. It’s particularly beneficial for those with larger setups or families who appreciate the stability of staying in one place.
3. Better Work-Life Balance for Remote Workers
Remote work has become increasingly common, and many professionals are taking their jobs on the road. While the flexibility is great, remote workers still need a reliable environment to get things done.
Monthly stays provide the predictability and consistency required for work. You’ll have time to learn the Wi-Fi strength, find the best working spots, and build a routine without disruption.
4. Opportunities to Build Community
Camping often brings people together, but it can be hard to form meaningful connections when you’re only around for a few nights. Monthly stays foster community. Over time, you’ll get to know your neighbors, campground hosts, and local residents.
5. Deeper Exploration of the Local Area
Most travelers barely scratch the surface of a destination before they move on. Staying for a month lets you go beyond the typical tourist attractions. You can:
Hike all the trails.
Visit hidden gems.
Discover local farmers markets and festivals.
Support small businesses.
Find the best coffee shop or breakfast joint.
6. Healthier Lifestyle & Better Routines
Short trips tend to revolve around quick food, busy days, and rushed mornings. Monthly camping encourages you to slow down and settle into healthier habits:
Cook fresh meals in your RV or at the campfire.
Get regular exercise through hiking, biking, or swimming.
Stick to a consistent sleep schedule.
Enjoy mindfulness in a natural setting.
7. Priority Access & Preferred Sites
Monthly reservations often come with perks that nightly stays do not. Some campgrounds offer priority access to the best sites or let long-term guests reserve far in advance.
Certain parks also provide discounts or incentives to long-term guests, such as:
8. Ideal for Seasonal & Transitional Living
Not everyone is on vacation. Many campers use monthly stays as a form of transitional or seasonal living:
Snowbirds head south for the winter to avoid cold climates.
Seasonal workers (e.g., construction crews, traveling nurses, or event staff) need short-term housing.
People relocating or house-hunting often use RV camping as a flexible bridge between homes.
9. Encourages Sustainable Travel
Frequent driving between destinations consumes more fuel and contributes to environmental impact. Monthly stays reduce your travel footprint while encouraging low-impact living.
You drive less.
You produce less waste from disposable travel items.
You become more mindful of your resource use (water, electricity, propane).
10. Peace of Mind & Emotional Comfort
There’s a psychological benefit to putting down temporary roots. It reduces decision fatigue, gives your body a chance to rest, and provides a sense of home—even if it’s a mobile one.
Campers who stay longer often feel more grounded and present. There’s less distraction, less rushing, and more time to simply enjoy the beauty of your surroundings.
Final Thoughts
Choosing to reserve a campsite for a month isn’t just about saving money—it’s about gaining time, space, and peace. Whether you’re a full-time RVer, remote worker, weekend adventurer, or seasonal traveler, there are countless benefits to slowing down and staying put.
Here’s a quick recap of what you gain with a monthly stay:
Lower cost per night
Less stress from moving frequently
A stable work/life routine
Opportunities to form community
Deeper exploration of your destination
Healthier habits and routines
Access to better campsites and amenities
Practical housing for transitional periods
More sustainable travel
A sense of emotional well-being
If you’re craving a more meaningful camping experience, it might be time to ditch the weekend rush and embrace the joy of staying longer. The road will always be there—but sometimes the real adventure is in slowing down.

“It’s my second full year and have enjoyed ALL the resorts such as Ocean Breeze, Maple Grove, and Old American. They are all very clean. There are always smiles on the staff with great weekend activities.”

“In 2001, my wife and I purchased a 2001 presidential 36′ fifth wheel. A short while after that, we found the K/M Resorts, looked at their camping program, liked it, and bought it. OVERVIEW
Mountain Shadows RV Park offers the finest camping in
Wells, Nevada!
Open All Year Around
Situated in the northeastern corner of the state among the Humboldt and Ruby Mountains, Mountain Shadows RV Park offers guests a quiet, family-oriented atmosphere in the beautiful countryside of Wells, Nevada. You'll find all the comforts of home as well as fun activities. Mountain Shadows RV Park welcomes families and large groups, offering spacious sites and lovely amenities. Come and enjoy the picturesque surroundings while you set up home base at Mountain Shadows RV Park .
For reservations call (775)752-3525.
Mountain Shadows RV Park is in the best setting for outdoor recreation. Wells is located next to the Humboldt and Ruby Mountains, allowing a great opportunity for hiking, biking, fishing, and more. There are several parks nearby, offering plenty of activities, including hiking, fishing, bird watching, and picnicking. Angle Lake features the Grays Lake trail, popular fishing spots where bass is abundant, and lots of native wildlife including mountain goats, bighorn sheep, deer, and antelope. ATV and equestrian trails are only a few minutes away leading to the Alpine lakes of the Ruby Mountains and the lower Humboldt range.
When you've had your fill of the outdoors, the town of Wells offers some intriguing attractions; as one of the first towns developed by the Transcontinental Railroad, Wells holds historic points of interest. Take a walking tour of the Old Town Front Street or visit the Metropolis Ghost Town, a once-booming farm town now dried up and abandoned with seven ranches and other building remnants still standing. There is also an Emigrant Trail Center that tells the story of Wells' participation in the Wild West. A nine-hole golf course, a casino, and fabulous restaurants are also worth visiting.
Although Mountain Shadows RV Park maintains a pleasant isolation from the hectic city, guests still have the convenience of attractions, a variety of activities, and city amenities. Whether you want to revel in Nevada's beautiful nature, or explore a charming historic town, your experience with Mountain Shadows RV Park will be a well-rounded and unique one.
For reservations call Mountain Shadows RV Park at (775) 752-3525.

We stayed at this park for 10 days and enjoyed our time very much. We had site 43 which is surrounded by amazing roses. The sunrise and set over the mountains was beautiful daily. Bathrooms were always well cared for and clean. Park staff does a great job of keeping things picked up and nice. Barb, in the office, is super helpful and friendly. Lots of good food choices in Mesquite. Had our anniversary dinner at Katerina In Castaway casino. Amazing prime rib! Park is within a half hour drive of Saint George, little over an hour to Zion, two hours to Cedar Breaks national monument. Great stay.
Sue B.
This RV park is AWESOME. My husband and I have been full-timers for 3 years and have traveled all over the country and this might be one of my favorite RV parks we've ever stayed in. The service is outstanding, the park is beautifully-kept with rose bushes and oleander and nice landscaping, it's clean, people are very polite and quiet, and it's so peaceful here. The clubhouse with the laundry room and showers is spotless. The WiFi is probably the fastest I've ever found at any RV park in the country. The spots are big and well-shaded. This place checks all our boxes, and it's close to gorgeous hiking, rock climbing, and mountains. Also, it's incredibly reasonably priced. Fantastic spot and will absolutely return! Totally a hidden gem. Barb and Shelly were both so helpful and nice with our reservations.
Emily R.
Nice and clean RV Park, very quiet, very clean showers and restrooms. Stayed here twice, on the way to Las Vegas and on the way back to St. George, it's located near the highway but far enough away to not hear the noise of it. Would definitely come back!
